title: The second-press window drains visibly in the rule under the prompt
body:
A first Ctrl+c or Ctrl+d arms a guard for `GUARD_WINDOW` (1.5 s), and the heavy rule under the prompt reads `press ^c again to quit` (`draw_guard_rule` in `ui.rs`). Nothing shows how much of the window is left, so the person cannot tell whether a second press will still count. coax-e81d6b adds the same guard for Esc.

## Proposal

- While a guard is armed, the rule after its message is a line of glyphs drawn in yellow, full when the guard arms. The glyphs disappear from the right as the window closes, back to the plain dim rule, which is gone when the window ends.
- The same drain shows for every guard: quit with Ctrl+c, quit with Ctrl+d, and cancel with Esc.
- coax redraws on its 150 ms tick while a guard is armed, so the drain moves smoothly enough at 1.5 s.

## Open

- The glyphs: the heavy rule's own `━` turning from yellow back to dim, or a distinct glyph such as `▰` that empties.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/bd10c4a0
notes.text: Jack, 2026-11-11: the drain uses the rule's own `━`, yellow while the window is open, turning back to dim from the right as it closes.
